name: How do I know if a lot is feasible for a custom home before buying it?

mainEntity.name: What should be checked before I buy land for a custom home in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should be checked before I buy land for a custom home in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A lot should be evaluated as a build site, not just as a property listing. Before purchasing land for a custom home in Los Angeles, buyers should confirm zoning, allowable floor area, setbacks, parking, access, utility connection points, slope, drainage, and any hillside or fire-related constraints. A soils or geotechnical review may be necessary if the site looks unstable or steep. Buyers should also study whether the lot will require demolition, retaining walls, easements, or special permit reviews that can affect both cost and timing. A strong feasibility review can reveal whether the dream design actually fits the lot before money is spent on architecture. This step is especially important in neighborhoods where lots are irregular, sloped, or surrounded by existing homes close to the property line. The best decision is made with a builder, designer, and civil or geotechnical consultant involved early.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before buying land, verify zoning, setbacks, access, utility availability, slope, soils, grading limits, and whether the lot triggers special reviews. A lot can look buildable but still be expensive or slow to develop because of site constraints. A feasibility review before purchase can prevent costly surprises.
